question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, fund accountant at Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III AIF, trust structure), is computing the fund-level tax liability on business income. Which effective rate does the workbook cite as the Maximum Marginal Rate (MMR) applicable to derivative (F&O) business income earned by a Category III AIF?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 14 explicitly states: 'Any gains arising from these [F&O] transactions shall be treated as Profits and Gains from Business and Profession and the fund should be liable to pay tax on such income at the MMR of Tax, i.e. 42.744%.' This is 30% base + 37% surcharge + 4% cess (or under the new 115BAC regime 30% + 25% surcharge + 4% cess). **The Trap:** 30% is the pre-surcharge base rate. 34.944% is the corporate non-concessional rate. 25.168% is the Section 115BAA concessional corporate rate. Only 42.744% includes the full MMR surcharge+cess stack for individuals/AOPs/BOIs. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D (Cat I/II) rarely sees MMR because pass-through routes income to investors at their own slab. XIX-C (All-Cat) covers both. XXI-B (PMS) does not see fund-level tax because PMS is pass-through by construction. XIX-E (here) drills MMR as the defining Cat III feature. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Before launching a new long-short strategy at Aravalli, price every basis point of alpha against the 42.744% fund-level MMR. An arbitrage desk showing 8% gross gives only ~4.6% to LPs — compare that realistically to a Cat I/II structure (pass-through) when pitching strategy IC papers.
